key_insight: Split complex-valued PINNs improve accuracy by learning amplitude and phase directly, reducing spectral bias on oscillatory and nonlinear PDEs.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a more robust surrogate for forward simulation and inverse parameter identification in fluid dynamics and wave-dominated systems.
method: Represent network weights and hidden states in the complex domain.
Apply split activations separately to real and imaginary parts for stability and efficiency.
Train on physics residuals plus data/collocation constraints across forward and inverse PDE benchmarks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports broad benchmarking on Burgers, Navier–Stokes, KdV, Schrödinger, Helmholtz, Poisson, cavity flow, Lorenz, and Beltrami flow, with Beltrami reaching a relative L2 error of 4.07 × 10^-5.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful choice of split activation and collocation sampling, so gains are not guaranteed without tuning.
paper_title: Split Complex-Valued Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Forward and Inverse Nonlinear PDEs
